clue.text: Man's rightwing background

parts.note: a man's thing is his
a Tory is a right-wing member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A conservative man's past is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's background is their past record or story, which is what this word means of a person.

clue.text: Dope starts exasperating leading lady

parts.note: dope is slang for a drug such as heroin

indicators.note: starts points to the first letter of exasperating

explanation.surface: A drug habit is beginning to infuriate the star actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes E, the first letter of 'exasperating', after HEROIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine is the principal female role in a story, its leading lady.

clue.text: For raising gratuities sacks old fighters

indicators.note: raising in a down clue means the word for gratuities is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: tips are gratuities
to fire someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: An employer dismisses staff for asking for more tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns TIPS upwards into SPIT in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spitfire was a British fighter aircraft of the Second World War.

clue.text: Which make people look down on pages?

definitions.text: Which make people look down on pages?

parts.words: Which make people look down on pages?
parts.note: the marks that point readers to the foot of a page, and that once flagged doubtful passages as despised

explanation.surface: A riddle about what makes people sneer at written pages.
explanation.walkthrough: An obelus (plural obeli) is the dagger sign used to refer the reader down to a footnote; it once marked a passage as spurious.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are printers' dagger signs, used to mark footnotes so readers glance down the page.

clue.text: Youth made US entry go astray

indicators.note: astray means off course, so the letters of US entry go are scrambled

explanation.surface: A young person's American visa application went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go astray' reads as a verb phrase, but 'go' is fodder and 'astray' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young person, the same as a youngster.

clue.text: Quote time in Leatherhead fortress

indicators.note: in says the word for time goes inside the word for quote

parts.note: to quote is to cite
AD (anno Domini) marks a time or era
the head, or first letter, of leather is L

explanation.surface: Someone cites the hour inside a stronghold in the Surrey town of Leatherhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Leatherhead is a real town in Surrey, England, but here it is split as the head of 'leather', its L. 'in' puts AD inside CITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a stronghold guarding a city, a kind of fortress.

clue.text: Dominic: Hilda's just a bit of a kid!

indicators.note: just a bit says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone tells Dominic that Hilda is only a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts with the C ending 'Dominic' and continues into 'Hilda'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kid is an informal word for a young person, a youngster.

clue.text: Actors I found in The Times

indicators.note: found in says the letter I goes inside the joined words that follow

parts.note: spans are periods of time

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a review of theatre performers in The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Times' looks like the newspaper, but 'The' is kept as it is and 'Times' becomes SPANS; 'found in' puts I inside THESPANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Thespians are performers, named after Thespis, the first Greek actor.

clue.text: Cleans street in the south of France up

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the whole sequence is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: sud is the French word for south

explanation.surface: Someone sweeps a road somewhere in Provence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the south of France' sounds like a region, but it gives SUD, French for south; 'up' turns STSUD round. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dust a room is to clean it by wiping away dust.

clue.text: Soporific air?

parts.note: a tune that sends listeners to sleep, read as a gentle song for a baby

explanation.definitionFit: A lullaby is a soothing song sung to make a child fall asleep, so a sleep-inducing tune.

clue.text: Hydrant contained brine, not soft running water

indicators.note: contained says the hydrant's letter is held within what is left of the other word
not says the letter for soft is taken away from brine

parts.note: B marks a soft (black) pencil lead, as H marks a hard one
H is the letter on signs marking a fire hydrant

explanation.surface: A fire hydrant was found to be holding salty water rather than soft water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes B (soft, as on a pencil) from BRINE, leaving RINE, and 'contained' puts H inside it. 'soft water' reads as a phrase but 'soft' is the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a major European river, so a body of running water.

clue.text: Catholic ruins veal pie

indicators.note: pie is printers' slang for jumbled type, so the letters of ruins veal are scrambled

explanation.surface: A vegetarian complaint that veal has spoilt a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' looks like the food but is the anagram signal: in printing, pie is type that has been mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic with a small c means all-embracing or general, a synonym.

clue.text: Violated by fiend running round circus

indicators.note: round says the scrambled fiend goes around the word for circus
running signals that the letters of fiend are set loose and rearranged

parts.note: a circus ring is the arena where the show takes place

explanation.surface: Someone was assaulted by a demon racing around a big top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges FIEND into INFED, and 'round' puts it around RING.
explanation.definitionFit: To infringe a rule or right is to break it, so violated is a synonym.

clue.text: Turkish governor's wooden-hearted father

indicators.note: hearted says the word for wooden is the heart, the inside, of the word for father

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
ash is a wood, standing here for something wooden

explanation.surface: An Ottoman official is described as a cold, unfeeling father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wooden-hearted' reads as unfeeling, but it says ASH sits in the heart of PA.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a high-ranking official, such as a provincial governor, in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Want front door removed from ground

indicators.note: removed says a letter is taken out of the word for want

parts.note: a dearth is a want or lack

indicators.note: front points to the first letter of door

explanation.surface: Someone wants their front door taken off and left on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front door' sounds like part of a house, but it is D, the front of 'door', removed from DEARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth means the soil or land underfoot, the ground.

clue.text: Employing a sucker to do some housework?

definitions.text: Employing a sucker to do some housework?

parts.words: Employing a sucker to do some housework?
parts.note: the sucker is a vacuum cleaner, named after a brand, rather than a gullible person

explanation.walkthrough: Hoover is a vacuum cleaner brand whose name became the everyday British verb for vacuuming.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English the brand name is a verb meaning to clean floors with a vacuum cleaner.

clue.text: Gruffly try to hail jockey

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre, so the letters of try to hail are moved about

explanation.surface: A rough-voiced attempt to call out to a racing jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jockey' looks like a rider to be hailed, but as a verb it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking from the throat gives a rough, husky voice, so it means gruffly.

clue.text: One's suffering pain? Cure him at surgery

indicators.note: at surgery suggests an operation that rearranges, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A patient in pain asks the doctor's surgery to fix him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at surgery' reads as a place, a British doctor's practice, but signals the anagram of CURE HIM AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who suffers from rheumatism, with aching joints, can be called a rheumatic.

clue.text: Disparity in main cable needing fixing

indicators.note: needing fixing says the letters of main cable are broken and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: An electrician spots an uneven load in the mains cable that must be repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing fixing' signals that MAIN CABLE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbalance is a lack of equality, a disparity.

clue.text: Scrubs mould without talking

indicators.note: without means outside, so the word for mould goes round the word for scrubs

parts.note: a die is a mould for shaping metal
to scour is to scrub, so scrubs is scours

explanation.surface: Someone silently cleans away mildew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside here: DIE goes round SCOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is spoken conversation or talk, used as a noun for talking.

clue.text: Fed up with notice outside church being vandalised

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word fed is read upwards, backwards
outside says the word for notice goes round the church abbreviation

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone sick of a church noticeboard has damaged it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' reads as annoyed, but 'up' turns FED into DEF; 'outside' puts AD round CE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deface something is to spoil its surface, an act of vandalism.

clue.text: So most of beer is not drunk?

indicators.note: most of says one letter of beer is dropped, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: A question about whether drinking only part of a beer keeps you sober.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops one E from BEER, leaving BER, after SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sober describes someone free of the effects of alcohol.

clue.text: Disorderly people roister indiscriminately

indicators.note: indiscriminately suggests a random order, so the letters of roister are mixed up

explanation.surface: A rowdy crowd revels without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indiscriminately' signals that ROISTER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who riot are unruly, disorderly people.

clue.text: Fellow umpire found Jack less sweet

indicators.note: less says the letter for jack is taken off the word for umpire

parts.note: an umpire is a judge in a contest
J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A colleague and a referee judged the jack less sugary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less sweet' reads as a phrase, but 'less' acts on JUDGE and 'sweet' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fudge is a soft confection, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Lifted excavated material

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue says the word for excavated is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: mined means dug out, excavated

explanation.surface: Earth that was dug up has been removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted' turns MINED upwards. 'excavated material' reads as spoil, but 'material' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton fabric, a material.

clue.text: Ordered admiral to look for animal

indicators.note: ordered here means put into a new arrangement, so the letters of admiral are rearranged

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: A naval commander was told to search for a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like a command given, but it rearranges ADMIRAL into ARMADIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured mammal of the Americas.

clue.text: Correct article to repair

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
to mend is to repair

explanation.surface: Someone corrects an item before having it fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text is to correct it.

clue.text: Road up-have flood

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the road abbreviation is read upwards

parts.note: to own is to have

explanation.surface: A road is dug up and then flooded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Road up' reads like roadworks, but 'up' turns RD into DR.
explanation.definitionFit: To drown land is to submerge it, to flood it.

clue.text: Sure prisoner will get depression if back inside

indicators.note: inside says the turned-round word goes within the prisoner and depression pair

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
a dent is a hollow or depression

indicators.note: back says the word if is read backwards

explanation.surface: A convict is promised he will be depressed if he goes back to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IF into FI, and 'inside' places it between CON and DENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To be confident is to be certain, so sure is a synonym.

clue.text: Getting round uncle left out cat

parts.note: a round shape is O

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is taken out of uncle

explanation.surface: Moving around, an uncle was left outside by the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' reads as one phrase, but 'left' gives L and 'out' removes it from UNCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat.

clue.text: Back late takes something to read, being spoilt

indicators.note: takes says the reversed word for late holds the reading matter
back says the word for late is read backwards

parts.note: late can mean dead, as in the late king
a mag, short for magazine, is something to read

explanation.surface: Someone returns late with a book and finds it ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns DEAD into DAED, and 'takes' puts MAG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something damaged has been harmed, which is to say spoilt.

clue.text: About five rabbits or bears

indicators.note: about says the word for rabbits goes around the numeral for five

parts.note: coneys is an old word for rabbits
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A count of roughly five rabbits, or perhaps some bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like the animal, but it is the verb meaning carries.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to carry or transport it, which is a synonym.
